Microsoft 365 security summary

This report checks your Microsoft 365 tenant against the security Baseline QIT Solutions applies to every tenant it manages, and shows what each further level adds. Each check shows whether your tenant passes today.

The first section lists the 15 Baseline checks that matter most, highest risk first. Each later section covers one further level: what it adds, the Microsoft license it needs, and 4 headline checks.

Conditional access replaces Microsoft's security defaults, so the same protection can be tuned by user, app and location. Administrators sign in with phishing-resistant methods, old sign-in protocols are blocked, and the passwords attackers try first are banned.

Reaching Managed needs Microsoft Entra ID P1, which Microsoft 365 Business Premium includes, and a project to deploy conditional access, starting in report-only mode.

Company devices are enrolled and encrypted, and the tenant can tell them apart from personal ones. Staff on a company laptop see fewer prompts, personal devices get limited browser access, and links and attachments are scanned before anyone opens them.

Reaching Protected needs Microsoft 365 Business Premium in use, not only licensed: Intune, Defender for Business and Defender for Office 365 Plan 1, deployed to every company device.

Risky sign-ins are challenged or blocked automatically, every sign-in uses a phishing-resistant method, and administrator access is granted only when needed. It usually covers administrators, finance and executives rather than the whole organisation.

Reaching Governed needs Microsoft Entra ID P2, or Microsoft 365 E5, for the people it covers, and a project to deploy risk policies and just-in-time administrator access.
